newsitem.title: UK: SCOTCH FIRMS FIGHT "WHITE WHISKEY" WITH EU RULES.
newsitem.headline: SCOTCH FIRMS FIGHT "WHITE WHISKEY" WITH EU RULES.

text.p: The Scotch Whisky Association (SWA) and two of the country's biggest drinks companies took a small distillery to court on Monday, claiming that its "white whiskey" was not whisky at all under European Union rules.

The Glen Killa Distillery on the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea between England and Ireland buys in whisky and then distills it once more to achieve a clear white spirit that it sells as Manx Whiskey, spelt in the Irish way with an "e".
The SWA, United Distillers, part of Guinness Plc, and Allied Domecq Plc want the court to rule that the drink should not be sold as whisky, however it is spelled.
Their lawyer, Simon Thorley, told the court that the 30,000 bottles of Manx Whiskey sold annually did not comply with European Union regulations covering whisky.
"It is important that the name is defended. Who knows what Cheddar cheese means now?" said SWA spokesman Campbell Evans.
The case is expected to last around 10 days. The judge will have to sample both Manx Whiskey and a selection of more traditional malts before coming to any conclusion.
